chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) regarding the saying of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله): “When a man commits adultery, the spirit of faith departs from him.”
“And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him.”
That is what departs from him.

key_terms.بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ: with a spirit from Him, meaning a divine support
key_terms.رُوحُ الْإِيمَانِ: the spirit of faith that supports the believer
key_terms.وَأَيَّدَهُمْ: He strengthened them or supported them
key_terms.يُفَارِقُهُ: departs from him or separates from him

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the spirit of faith leaves a person when he commits adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the departure of the spirit of faith at the time of adultery refers to the divine support mentioned in the Quranic phrase, “And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him.” It connects the Prophetic hadith to a Quranic expression, showing that sinful action causes a person to lose a special divine aid associated with iman.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,
‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws regarding the words of Rasool-Allahsaww: ‘When the man commits adultery, the spirit of the Emān separates from him’.
[58:22] and He has Supported them with a Spirit from Him.
That is which separates from him’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr who has said the following:
“Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) about the words of the Messenger of Allah, ‘When a person commits fornication the spirit of belief departs him,’
the Imam said, ‘It is mentioned in His (Allah) words,
‘He has supported them with a spirit from Him,’
that is the spirit that departs him.’”
